research_scope: Source-free whole-formulation-anchored review of shared prerequisite identities; no source/definition mutation, no parent-definition equivalence, no freeze or gate change.

aliases.reason: The affine-hull intersection variant takes the intersection of all affine-closed supersets of S, and the topological-closure variant takes the intersection of all topologically closed supersets of A. Their shared prerequisite is the arbitrary intersection of a family of subsets of a fixed universe; the different closure predicates determine distinct indexing families in the parent definitions.

Both discrete-martingale variants require equality of conditional-expectation and process random variables P-almost surely rather than pointwise. One quantifies over adjacent indices n,n+1; the other over all n≤m. Their common missing prerequisite is almost-sure equality of two real random variables; the different quantifier ranges and martingale identities remain distinct mathematical parent formulations.

The locally-nilpotent-ideal and Jacobson-ring sources use commutative rings with multiplicative identity, just as the prime-ideal and Noetherian-module sources explicitly do. They share the associative commutative unital coefficient-ring prerequisite. Nilpotence, radical-ideal and Noetherian module restrictions remain separately attached to their parent statements.

The division-ring source requires a nonzero associative unital ring D and therefore names its two-sided identity 1_D; the unit-of-ring source uses the same two-sided multiplicative identity 1_R in a general associative unital ring. The additional 1_D≠0 restriction follows from the nonzero division-ring parent hypothesis, not a different definition of multiplicative identity.
